title: The US and China alone are a quarter of the $126 trillion world economy
intro: Nominal GDP of the ten largest economies, IMF World Economic Outlook estimates (2026). World total: $126.3 trillion.

altInsight: The United States ($32.4tn) and China ($20.9tn) together account for roughly a quarter of the $126.3 trillion world economy, far ahead of Germany ($5.5tn) in third place.

source.name: IMF World Economic Outlook estimates, via Wikipedia 'List of countries by GDP (nominal)'

_routing.gate0: GDP by country is a magnitude/ranking claim (largest economies) → bar/column family (FT Visual Vocabulary: magnitude → bar, ranking → sorted bar).
_routing.gate1: STATIC wins — one claim (who is biggest), ~10 rows, cross-channel, core insight annotatable directly. No interaction needed to read the ranking.
_routing.gate2: NOT triggered — no personal-data 'find your country' hook is the purpose, dataset is small (10 rows), not web-only.
_routing.gate3: NOT triggered — a static ranking is not irreducibly sequential; no single chart evolving across 4+ states; a plain magnitude ranking has no author-mandated scroll order.
_routing.gate4: NOT triggered — no temporal diffusion / motion-is-the-encoding; this is a single-year snapshot, not a spread over time; distribution not mandated social/vertical.
_routing.gate5: TRIGGERED (geographic data: per-country). Condition assessment: (1) spatial pattern is NOT the story — the story is a RANKING of magnitudes ('largest economies'), an explicit Gate 5 BAR signal; (2) value is NOT map-safe — nominal GDP is a RAW ABSOLUTE COUNT ($), which on a choropleth would merely redraw the population/economy-size map (the guard against absolute counts fires); (3) regions are legible but that alone never earns a map. Two independent reasons to fall back to bar: ranking framing AND raw-absolute-count value. → sorted bar chart, producer dw-chart.
_routing.color_rationale: Subject is the economy/growth — Okabe-Ito green #009E73 (growth/value signal) over the default blue, which is reserved for water/cold subjects. CVD-safe.
_routing.honesty_note: The requested Visual Capitalist article URL returned HTTP 403 and all archive/proxy fallbacks were unreachable, so its 2025 figures could NOT be extracted (no fabrication). Figures here are the fetchable IMF estimates from Wikipedia's 'List of countries by GDP (nominal)', which the page labels IMF (2026) — NOT the article's 2025 numbers, and NOT the $117tn headline. World total is $126.3tn on this source. Source cite is honest to what was actually fetched.
